headline: China escalates gray-zone pressure on Taiwan

CGA condemned it as 'maritime harassment' amounting to…
sources: Taiwan Coast Guard Administration (CGA) statement via Liberty Times / galaxytvonline; Taiwan MND X posts (MoNDefense, Oct 19)
fault_line: Gray-zone pressure or slow-motion invasion — is China already at war with Taiwan without firing a shot?

sections.what_happened: Taiwan's coast guard on Sunday drove away 16 Chinese vessels (coast guard ships, research vessels, 4 fishing boats) operating simultaneously off Hualien, Pingtung, Kaohsiung and around Pratas (Dongsha); some entered Taiwan's restricted waters. CGA condemned it as 'maritime harassment' amounting to 'hybrid warfare' and 'fake law enforcement to actually expand jurisdiction.' Taiwan MND reported Monday 5 PLA aircraft + 6 PLAN vessels + 9 official ships, with 2 sorties crossing the median line into the ADIZ. CGA data: 244 Chinese vessels around Taiwan in July vs 55 in June, 30 in May; 152 in first 21 days of August. China TAO warned Taiwan must 'bear the consequences' of the Oct 1 water-cannon incident.
sections.what_verified: Multiple outlets (Economic Times/ANI, Lokmat Times, Galaxy TV, NOCUTNEWS/Yonhap) carry the same MND/CGA figures; Ryan D. Martinson (US Naval War College) corroborates research-vessel escalation scale as 'unprecedented.' TaiwanDefence notes coast-guard-lead doctrine for militia crossings.
sections.what_disputed: China TAO: Taiwan is 'roughly handling Chinese vessels in a dangerous manner' and 'stoking cross-strait confrontation'; Beijing insists patrols are lawful enforcement in its waters.
sections.why_matters: Beijing's pressure campaign is quantifiable now: 244 vessels in July, 16 driven off in one day. Map-explainer material — the four simultaneous zones are the story. Note the water-cannon incident (Oct 1) as the trigger China cites.
sections.context: Background: China escalates gray-zone pressure on Taiwan: 16 vessels driven away, CGA calls it 'hybrid warfare'; record vessel counts

totw_analysis: Our read: Beijing's pressure campaign is quantifiable now: 244 vessels in July, 16 driven off in one day. Map-explainer material — the four simultaneous zones are the story. Note the water-cannon incident (Oct 1) as the trigger China cites.
